section_summary.extract_value: This subsection describes how body dissatisfaction (actual-ideal weight discrepancy) was measured using the Photographic Figure Rating Scale (Swami et al., 2008c), presenting 10 greyscale images and asking participants to select current and ideal figures. Ratings were made on a 10-point scale and body dissatisfaction was operationalised as the absolute difference between current and ideal ratings. The section does not mention Study 1, Experiment 2, multiple sample subsets, sample size, demographics, BMI measurements, or body appreciation (BAS/BAS-2).
section_summary.evidence_source: Quoted sentences: "To measure actual-ideal weight discrepancy, we used the Photographic Figure Rating Scale (Swami et al. 2008c), a figural rating scale in which participants are presented with 10 photographic images of women ranging in body size from emaciated to obese." and "Ratings were made on a 10-point scale (1 = Figure with the lowest BMI, 10 = Figure with the highest BMI). For the purposes of analyses, we operationalised body dissatisfaction as the difference between unsigned (absolute) current and ideal ratings..."
